_heading_rule_derivation: measured 2026-08-29 on the two freshest C1 shards (ais_2026-08-28 + ais_2026-08-29, SOG>=7 fixes, 20-deg bins): box 0 San Pedro — outbound mode 180-200 (10.1%), open water S/SW of the bay; inbound (320-060) excluded -> 130-300. box 1 NY approach — E+S departure semicircle kept (modes 180-220 = 18.0%, 60-100 = 11.5%), NW harbor-approach quadrant excluded -> 60-210. box 2 Rotterdam — cleanly bimodal (44.4% E inbound vs 41.2% W/NW outbound), port E of box, sea W/NW -> 240-340. box 3 Singapore Strait — through-traffic bimodal and BOTH directions are legitimate 72 h departures (E/NE modes 40-80 = 21.5% + 120-140 = 9.2%; W mode 240-260 = 22.6%) -> two ranges 30-150 and 220-310, port-approach quadrants excluded. An eligibility filter derived from one two-day measurement and pinned here; any change is an amendment, never a tuning.
corridor_rule: constant COG/SOG rhumb-line extrapolation from the most recent position report; 72 one-hour bins at bin midpoints; full declaration in corpus_intake/f1_optimizer_settings.json (corridor_rule)

gefs_retrieval.retrieval_path_v04: Amendment A4 (2026-08-29): credential-free HTTPS range-fetch from the public NOAA bucket against the repo-archived cycle manifests — each manifest carries the original object key, the UGRD/VGRD byte range, and the sha256 of exactly those bytes; fetched bytes are digest-verified against the repo pin BEFORE decode. CC measurement 2026-08-29: HTTP 206, 540,805 B, digest exactly the repo pin. Stronger than the previously assumed credentialed route (R2 env vars presence-checked NOT SET, values never read) because the digest is pinned before the fetch.
